title: A split-and-merge passage preserves one source identity through two branches
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED. A complete passage first divides one bound source into two portions, applies distinct whole-form operations, then recombines the portions. Directed whole-form composition predicts that the merge operation receives both branch outputs from the same source, a stronger consequence than shared adjacency or a repeated word.

design.mechanism: branching participant identity with a typed merge destination
design.structural_basis: The known composition baseline permits ordered whole-form residuals and context-conditioned roles; GDT697 distinguishes a true action-output chain from two actions sharing only a destination.
design.passage_contract: A candidate source must explicitly describe one initial participant, two separately operated portions, and a later recombination or common result. The target candidate must contain complete groups for source, both branch operations, and merge; absent roles remain UNKNOWN.
design.prediction: The two branch outputs remain linked to one initial source and both are consumed by the later merge whole. A model that assigns independent singleton referents, nearest-left ownership, or simple coordination should fail at least one branch-to-merge edge.
design.smallest_test: Use one independently bound split-and-merge source and a predeclared set of complete target passage candidates. Freeze branch order and merge position, then check source identity and two incoming edges separately; include a no-merge and nearest-neighbor control.
design.strongest_likely_failure: The apparent split is merely two adjacent operations on unrelated items, or the merge is a generic closure marker that does not receive either branch output. A single shared destination can be mistaken for true recombination.
design.falsifier: No candidate binds both branch outputs to one source and one merge, or nearest-neighbor/coordination controls provide the same edge coverage, or the source narrative does not force recombination.
design.source_binding: Required: an independently fixed complete account with explicit division, separate treatment, and recombination. The source must state whether recombination is physical, logical, or merely co-location; target forms cannot decide that distinction.
prior_distinctions: GDT697 has one serial bridge and one repeated shared destination but no branch-and-merge test
IDEA000032 concerns a coordination marker over a list
IDEA000068 concerns one identity through transformation without two branch outputs
design.access: Already admitted exposed sources only; no new target page, reserve, f84/f84r, or f116v access. Use guarded selector-first TSV queries if a bounded occurrence census is later selected.
design.selection_status: raw_unreviewed; no independent meaning, target success, or decoder claim
